prerequisites.concept: Exact saturation of the jet semigroup

evidence.quote: The adjoint lifting statement below uses these data but does *not* assume that $c_0$ itself lies in the interior of $K$.
The slice bound used only the definition of $M_n$, so the argument assumes no same-dimensional ODP estimate.

outputs.exact_statement:
Let $n\ge2$, and let $x$ be a singular closed point of a normal complex algebraic $n$-fold $X$. Suppose that $K_X$ is $\mathbb Q$-Cartier and that $X$ is klt near $x$, with zero boundary. Then $$\widehat{\operatorname{vol}}(x,X)\le2(n-1)^n.$$ Equality holds if and only if $$(X,x)_{\mathrm{an}}\cong
 \left(\{z_0^2+\cdots+z_n^2=0\}\subset\mathbb C^{n+1},0\right).$$

Let $V$ be an $n$-dimensional K-semistable $\mathbb Q$-Fano variety, where $n\ge2$. If $V$ is singular, then $$(-K_V)^n\le
       2\left(\frac{n^2-1}{n}\right)^n<2n^n.$$ If $V\not\cong\mathbb P^n$, then $(-K_V)^n\le2n^n$, with equality precisely when $V$ is a smooth quadric $Q^n\subset\mathbb P^{n+1}$ or $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^{n-1}$. These two descriptions coincide for $n=2$.
Let $y\in Y$ be an $N$-dimensional klt germ, where $N\ge1$. Then $$d((y,0),Y\times\mathbb A^1)\le d(y,Y).$$

Let $v$ be a finite-discrepancy valuation of a klt germ, with finitely generated positively graded associated graded ring $\mathop{\mathrm{gr}}_v R$. Then $$\mathop{\mathrm{edim}}(R)\le\mathop{\mathrm{edim}}(\mathop{\mathrm{gr}}_v R).$$
For $n\ge2$, the ordinary double point $Q_n$ has $$\widehat{\operatorname{vol}}(0,Q_n)=2(n-1)^n.$$

Let $x$ be a singular closed point of a normal complex algebraic fourfold $X$. Suppose that $K_X$ is $\mathbb Q$-Cartier and $X$ is klt near $x$, with zero boundary. Then $$\widehat{\operatorname{vol}}(x,X)\le162.$$ Equality holds if and only if the complex analytic germ is $$\left(\{z_0^2+z_1^2+z_2^2+z_3^2+z_4^2=0\},0\right).$$ No isolatedness, complete-intersection, quotient, or smoothability assumption is made.

Under [cone:eq-induction], there is a singular K-polystable Fano cone $C=\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}S$, with vertex $o$, such that $$d(o,C)=d(x,X),\qquad \mathop{\mathrm{edim}}(X,x)\le\mathop{\mathrm{edim}}(C,o).$$ The puncture $C\setminus\{o\}$ is smooth, $S$ is a normal Gorenstein ring, and its canonical module has a homogeneous generator. The cone has zero boundary.

There are primitive positive integral cocharacters $\zeta_i$, of canonical weights $r_i=A(\zeta_i)\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$, such that $$\label{cone:eq-fast}
             \zeta_i=\frac{r_i}{n}\xi+\epsilon_i,\qquad
             \epsilon_i\longrightarrow0$$ in the real cocharacter space. If the ray of $\xi$ is rational, the sequence may be chosen constant and exact. Otherwise $r_i\to\infty$.*

*The normalized volumes of the degree valuations $\operatorname{wt}_{\zeta_i}$ tend to $\widehat{\operatorname{vol}}(o,C)$. For any fixed finite set of homogeneous algebra generators, their $\zeta_i$-degrees lie between $cr_i$ and $Cr_i$ for positive constants $c,C$. Consequently the largest stabilizer order $m_{\max,i}$ on the puncture is $O(r_i)$.

For a primitive positive integral grading $\zeta$, of canonical weight $r$, let $$B=[(C\setminus\{o\})/\mathbb G_m].$$ Then $B$ is a smooth effective proper orbifold of dimension $N$, with projective coarse space $\mathop{\mathrm{Proj}}S$. It has a faithful ample weight-one line bundle $L$ such that $$\label{cone:eq-section-ring}
         S_j=H^0(B,jL),\qquad -K_B=rL.$$ Every stabilizer is a finite cyclic group. At a point of order $m$, a smooth transverse uniformizer carries a faithful $\mu_m$-action, and $L$ has a faithful fiber character.

Let $\zeta_i$ be primitive positive integral gradings satisfying $$\zeta_i=\frac{r_i}{n}\xi+\epsilon_i,
 \qquad r_i=A(\zeta_i),\qquad \|\epsilon_i\|\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad m_{\max}(\zeta_i)\leq\frac{r_i}{N}.
 \label{small:fast-sequence}$$ For all sufficiently large $i$, every stabilizer is trivial and $r_i\in\{N,N+1\}$. More precisely, the polarized quotient is $$(B_i,L_i)\cong
 \begin{cases}
  (\mathbb P^N,\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^N}(1)),&r_i=N+1,\\
  (Q^N,\mathcal O_{Q^N}(1)),&r_i=N,
 \end{cases}$$ where $Q^N\subset\mathbb P^{N+1}$ is a smooth quadric. Consequently the cone $C$ is respectively smooth or an ordinary double point. The assertion includes the constant exact primitive grading when the ray of $\xi$ is rational.

Let $b_1',\ldots,b_n'\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$ represent the characters of $\mu_m$ on $T_{C,P}$, with the trivial character represented by $m$. Every component through $F$ of the scheme of homogeneous maps $F':\mathbb A^2(1,m)\to C$ satisfying $F'(0,1)=P$ has dimension at least $$\chi=n+\frac rm-\sum_{j=1}^n\frac{b_j'}m.
 \label{small:chi}$$ In particular this dimension is at least $n$, except possibly when $r/m=N$ and the entire tangent action at $P$ is trivial.
The morphism in Equation [small:evaluation] is finite and surjective. Its fiber over $o$ is supported at the unique contracted map.
Let $b$ be the degree of the finite evaluation in Lemma 12. There is a nonzero algebraic section $$s\in H^0(C^\circ,\mathop{\mathrm{Sym}}^bT_{C^\circ})$$ of integral-grading weight $-bm$.
Let $b\geq1$, and let $s$ be a nonzero homogeneous algebraic section of $\mathop{\mathrm{Sym}}^bT_{C^\circ}$, of $\xi$-weight $\tau$, with vector fields weighted as derivations. Then $$\tau\geq-b.$$

There is a constant $c>0$ with the following property for all sufficiently close gradings in Equation [small:fast-sequence]. If a nonzero rank-$b$ tensor on $C^\circ$ has integral-grading weight $-bm$, with $m>0$, then it has a nonzero torus eigencomponent of character $\chi$ satisfying $$\|\chi\|\leq cb.$$ Consequently, if the tensor is as in Lemma 13, then $$m\leq\frac rn+c\|\epsilon\|. \label{small:m-bound}$$

Along the fixed-cone sequence of gradings, there are numbers $\eta_
u\ge0$ tending to zero such that $$\label{jet:moment-inequalities}
 H\ge rac2s,\qquad
 \mathbb E[(1+B_0(X))e^{-B_0(X)}]\ge-\eta_
u H.$$ For an exact minimizing rational grading one may take $\eta_
u=0$.

A nonzero mean-zero linear combination of independent mean-one exponentials has a positive continuous log-concave density on the whole real line. Adding further independent scaled exponentials, with either sign of coefficient, preserves these properties. If $Z$ has such a density, then $$\label{prob:grunbaum}
 \frac1e\le\mathbb P(Z\le\mathbb EZ)\le1-\frac1e.$$

Let $Z$ have a positive log-concave probability density on $\mathbb R$, and let $E$ be an independent mean-one exponential. If $$\mathbb E k(Z+c_*E)=0,$$ then $\mathbb E k(Z+cE)>0$ for every $c<c_*$ and $\mathbb E k(Z+cE)<0$ for every $c>c_*$.

Let $\mathcal X$ be a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack over $\mathbb C$, with trivial generic stabilizer and projective coarse space. Let $\Theta$ be an effective rational divisor with simple normal crossing support and coefficients less than one. If $D$ is a Cartier divisor and $D-(K_{\mathcal X}+\Theta)$ is nef and big, then $$H^q(\mathcal X,\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}(D))=0\qquad(q>0).$$

For the orbifold jet data above, $$\label{adj:adjoint-implication}
 (j,\alpha)\in\Lambda,\qquad
 (j,\alpha)+c_0\in\mathop{\mathrm{int}}K
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad (j,\alpha)\in\Gamma.$$

Suppose $c_0\in\mathop{\mathrm{int}}K$. Then the following statements hold:* 1. *$K$ is a rational polyhedral cone.* 2. *Every facet has a primitive nonnegative support form $\eta\in\Lambda^*$ satisfying $\eta(c_0)=1$.* 3. *The semigroup and its interior lattice points satisfy $$\label{adj:saturation-identities} \Gamma=K\cap\Lambda, \qquad \mathop{\mathrm{int}}K\cap\Lambda=c_0+\Gamma.$$* *In particular, $\Gamma$ is a finitely generated saturated affine semigroup with group $\Lambda$. These conclusions apply to every sufficiently far grading and chosen point covered by Theorem 23, including its exact rational case.
Under Equation [filt:volume-hypothesis], $D$ is reduced.

Let $E$ be a finitely generated positively graded reduced equidimensional Cohen–Macaulay $\mathbb C$-algebra of dimension $N\geq2$, with $E_0=\mathbb C$ and $\mathop{\mathrm{Hilb}}E(z)=(1-z)^{-N}$. If the grading action has trivial stabilizer at every nonvertex closed point of $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}E$, then $E$ is a polynomial ring on $N$ generators of degree one.
There is a nonvertex closed point of $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}D$ whose $T$-grading stabilizer has order $h\geq2$.

There is a normal Gorenstein algebraic germ $y\in Y$ of dimension $n$, preserved by $\mu_h$, with a nonzero function $\lambda_Y\in\mathfrak m_{Y,y}$ of character $-1$, such that $Y$ is klt away from $\lambda_Y=0$. Every quasi-monomial valuation $u$ centered at $y$ gives a quasi-monomial valuation $w$ centered at $o\in C$. Writing $\ell=u(\lambda_Y)>0$, one has $$\label{boot:basic-test}
 A_C(w)\leq N\ell+A_Y(u),
 \qquad
 \mathop{\mathrm{vol}}(w)\leq \ell^{-n}.$$ The comparison is valid before klt at $y$ has been established.
The germ $y\in Y$ is klt.
The germ $y\in Y$ is singular.

Let $R=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ and let $\mathfrak a_t=\{g\in R:u_*(g)\geq t\}$. For every character $\chi\in\mathbb Z/h\mathbb Z$, $$\dim_\mathbb C(R/\mathfrak a_t)_\chi
 =\frac{\sigma}{h\,n!}t^n+o(t^n)
 \qquad(t\longrightarrow\infty).$$

Assume the local ODP volume theorem in all dimensions smaller than $n$. Then $M_n\leq p_n$. Equivalently, every singular boundary-zero klt $n$-dimensional germ satisfies $$\widehat{\operatorname{vol}}(x,X)\leq 2(n-1)^n.$$

One has $h=2$, $d(y,Y)=p_n$, and $A'=N\ell$. After rescaling $u_*$ so that $\ell=1$, the resulting restriction $w$ satisfies $$\label{boot:equality-identities} A'=N, \qquad \sigma=2, \qquad A_C(w)=2N, \qquad \mathop{\mathrm{vol}}(w)=2^{-N}, \qquad w=\frac{2N}{n}\operatorname{wt}_\xi.$$ The optimal splitting fraction in Equation [boot:refined-volume] is $x=1/2$, and all inequalities producing that estimate are equalities at the level of leading coefficients.
In the normalization of Lemma 40, the section $v\in S_m$ used to define the two filtrations satisfies $w(v)\leq2$.
Along the fast gradings of the fixed equality cone, the large-stabilizer construction implies $Nm_{\max}\leq r$ for every sufficiently far term.
If a singular cone obtained in Proposition 7 satisfies $d(o,C)=p_n$, then it is the standard ordinary double point cone.

If $x\in X$ is a singular klt hypersurface germ of dimension $n\ge2$, then $$\widehat{\operatorname{vol}}(x,X)\le2(n-1)^n.$$ If equality holds, the quadratic part of a local equation is nondegenerate, and $(X,x)$ is analytically an ordinary double point.
